CLEAR DOME: a pure unbroken arc of deep blue stretching from edge to edge, smooth and open across the full vault
CLEAN BLUE SKY: an even wash of bright blue filling the dome, crisp and open with a gentle deepening toward the zenith
OPEN SKY: a wide uninterrupted blue canopy, saturated at the top and softening toward the horizon into a paler hue
CLEAR VAULT: a polished dome of solid blue, deepening overhead and easing to a softer pale band at the far rim
EMPTY BLUE DOME: a seamless blue arc overhead, rich and deep at the crown, fading to a thin luminous pale blue at the edges
TALL CUMULUS: great white soft cloud heaps stacking up over the horizon, flat grey bases, sunlit crowns, small blue gaps between
STACKED CLOUD HEAPS: massive rounded heaps of white cloud building high, their bases broad and dark, upper cauliflower tops brilliant white
BILLOWING COLUMNS: enormous cloud pillars rising and expanding upward, each tower rounded and bright, piling into a grand heap of white
CLOUD CASTLES: several tall soft cumulus formations rising side by side, their sculpted domes and turrets gleaming against the blue behind them
RISING CUMULUS: a single vast tall soft cloud heaps climbing high, its flanks shaded cool grey, its upper dome blazing white and swelling outward
HIGH CIRRUS: thin feathery streaks of ice cloud drawn lightly across the upper sky, translucent and bright, curving at their tips
MACKEREL SKY: a high rippled sheet of small cloud scales across most of the sky, thin enough to glow
CIRRUS VEIL: a pale gauzy layer of high ice-crystal cloud spread wide, giving the sky a soft milky luminance from edge to edge
MARE'S TAILS: long curling filaments of cirrus trailing across the upper sky, each wisp stretched thin by high winds aloft
DISTANT STORM LINE: a low dark band of storm cloud lying along the far horizon, its top soft and ragged, spreading wide beneath a clearer sky above
DISTANT RAIN CURTAIN: a grey veil of falling rain hanging beneath a heavy cloud base far away, the curtain soft and trailing toward the ground
FAR SQUALL LINE: a long dark cloud band pressing along the distant sky, beneath it a blurred curtain of rain streaming downward in soft grey sheets
CLOUD CAP: a moist feathered cloud draping softly over a high summit, clinging and spreading gently at its edges in damp wisps
CAPPING CLOUD: a thick moist cloud settling over a peak, its edges feathering outward and downward in soft trailing tendrils that cling and breathe
SUMMIT VEIL: a moist cloud cap resting over a high point, its feathered fringe spilling softly down the upper slopes in quiet drifting layers
BANDED GRADIENT SKY: the sky shading in broad arching bands from deep blue overhead through softer mid tones, a few small puffs scattered below
LAYERED SKY: smooth colour bands arc across the dome from rich blue at the top to a paler tint below, small rounded clouds floating in the lower band
GRADIENT ARC: a gently banded sky curving from intense blue at the zenith down through softer layers, dotted here and there with small bright cloud puffs
MILKY WAY ARCH: a broad river of cold starlight arching across the dark sky, thousands of stars packed into a glowing band, scattered bright points all around
STAR FIELD: the full dome dusted with countless stars, the Milky Way a bright dense arch of silver mist curving from one horizon to the other
